children.text: The South African tourist visa allows the holder a short-term tourist visit to South Africa.

To obtain a South African tourist visa, a visit to the South African consulate in Turkey is required. First, the required documentation must be gathered and the visa application completed, after which a consulate appointment date is scheduled.
The consulate schedules appointments in two ways: a) by sending the applicant an exact appointment date by email, or b) by arranging it with the applicant over a phone call.

page.title: What is the process for obtaining the visa?

children.text: Processing of the South Africa visa application begins once the documents are submitted, and takes 10 to 15 business days.

The tourist (sticker) visa is generally issued for the exact period the applicant has indicated in the application and supporting documents.
In general, the visa allows a stay in South Africa of at least 30 days, but this is entirely at the consul's discretion.

page.title: How long is the visa valid?

children.text: Confirmation of the consulate appointment booking
Visa application form
Passport (valid for at least 6 more months)
Flight reservation
Proof of accommodation
Police clearance certificate
Additional documentation (invitation letter, motivation letter, and others)
Make sure to include all required information in your application.
Make sure your passport is valid for at least six months from your planned return date.
If you have additional supporting documents, submit them to the consulate translated and certified.
Apply for your visa at least 1 month before your trip, as the consulate handles a high volume of applications.
The consulate reserves the right to request additional documentation from the applicant.
It's important to remember, and not exceed, the rights and obligations granted by your visa category.

If you have traveled to any of the following countries: Angola, Benin, Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Ethiopia, Gabon, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Kenya, Libya, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone, South Sudan, Sudan, Togo, Uganda, Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Suriname, Trinidad and Tobago, or Venezuela — you will additionally need proof of a yellow fever vaccination.

content.text: What are my chances of getting a visa?

children.text: It's difficult to predict the likelihood of a specific applicant being granted a visa. However, it's clear that this depends on your close ties to your home country. Clear proof of your travel purpose is also important.

content.text: Does the eConsul guarantee the visa?

children.text: No one else can interfere with the consul's decision on issuing a visa. This decision is final. However, our qualified professionals will do everything possible to prepare your documents properly and in your favor for the consulate, so the consul fully understands your current circumstances and prospects, which increases the likelihood of the visa being granted.
